cohort: The study included 78 young women with gestational trophoblastic neoplasias who underwent fertility-sparing uterine lesion resection at Peking Union Medical College Hospital.
finding: Fertility-sparing uterine lesion resection resulted in complete remission in all patients, with high rates of pregnancy (83.8%) and live birth (77.4%) among those attempting conception, and a tumor size greater than 4.2cm was found to be an independent risk factor for recurrence.
mod_finding: Uterine rupture did not occur in patients, regardless of whether they had a cesarean section or vaginal delivery.
